text:
Maya (CS): Strandline is aiming to go live on Redwood Private next Tue 07:00 PT. Preflight chat  wanted to capture network, IAM, KMS, and audit pipeline checks. Drop status or blockers.

Strandline Ops: Dry-run Friday. Two major asks: 1) can audit logs be delivered to our Splunk ingest via S3 (cross-account), 2) we need clear KMS ownership semantics  legal requires that keys can be transferred/rotated under customer control after 90 days.

Liam (Network): For connectivity we support either VPC peering or PrivateLink. Peering is simplest network-wise; PrivateLink gives stronger isolation. Which does Strandline prefer for initial traffic?

Strandline Ops: Peering for now. Keep PrivateLink as a follow-up. We'll need explicit route table entries and the maintenance IPs for scheduled patch windows.

Ruben (SRE): From SRE checklist: establish peering + propagate routes, confirm egress/NAT paths for outbound callbacks, validate internal DNS names resolve to peered IPs, ensure our health-check endpoint (tcp/8443 + tls) is reachable. Our quick test: `openssl s_client -connect 10.45.12.8:8443 -servername api.redwood.internal` then `curl --header "X-Redwood-Test: smoke" https://api.redwood.internal/health`.

Isha (Security): KMS guidance: we strongly recommend customer-managed CMKs in their account. If they need transferability after 90 days, that's fine but requires a key policy that allows Redwood's cross-account service role and also a documented handoff process. Example key grant snippet we’ll provide. Also: audit events must be logged to CloudTrail (for KMS events) and S3 write events. If you plan Splunk ingestion via S3, ensure Glue/Lambda forwarder has read permissions to the bucket.

Strandline Ops: Splunk pipeline: yes S3 -> Lambda forwarder -> Splunk HEC. We'll provide the bucket and ARN. Need the S3 put policy and the assume-role ARN for Redwood. Also retention/immutability ask: some records must be WORM for 5 years (we use S3 Object Lock compliance mode). Can Redwood write to Object Lock enabled buckets?

Isha (Security): Object Lock in compliance mode requires the writer to have special permissions and retention mode set on put. We can write to it if you grant PutObjectRetention and PutObjectLegalHold to the Redwood role. Note it may complicate deletion/rollbacks. We'll document the exact policy.

Maya (CS): Action items: 1) Liam to post CIDR ranges and Terraform snippet for peering, 2) Isha to post CMK policy + S3 trust policy templates, 3) Ruben to produce smoke test steps and a small dashboard of golden signals for post-cutover (error-rate, p50/p95 latency, token consumption). Parasol? (typo: Strandline confirm)

Strandline Ops: Confirmed. Bucket ARN: arn:aws:s3:::strandline-redwood-ingest. Retention: 5y WORM, SSE-KMS using our CMK `alias/strandline-audit`. Legal: we need contractual note on KMS ownership rollover at 90 days.

onboard-bot: Checklist created: vpc-peering, route-entries, nat/egress, dns-resolve, healthcheck, cmk-policy, s3-trust-role, object-lock-perms, post-cut-dashboard. Status: 0/9.

Liam (Network): Posting Terraform snippet for peering (apply in your account):

```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "redwood_strandline" {
  provider = aws.redwood
  vpc_id = "vpc-redwood-prod"
  peer_vpc_id = "vpc-strandline-prod"
  peer_region = "us-west-2"
  auto_accept = false
}
```

Liam (Network): I'll paste the maintenance CIDRs in 10m.

Isha (Security): CMK policy example (redacted):

```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Sid":"AllowStrandlineUse","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::REDCLOUD:role/redwood-service-role"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"*"}]}
```

Isha (Security): S3 bucket trust role (snippet):

```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::REDCLOUD:role/redwood-s3-writer"},"Action":["s3:PutObject","s3:PutObjectRetention","s3:PutObjectLegalHold"],"Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::strandline-redwood-ingest/*"}]}
```

Ruben (SRE): Post-cut KPIs we'll watch: 1) 5xx error rate < 0.5% sustained, 2) auth failures < 0.1% of requests, 3) p95 latency < 800ms for typical prompt sizes, 4) token cost per minute baseline not exceeding 20% spike. I'll create a small Grafana board and a PagerDuty rule if error-rate > 1% for 5m.

Strandline Ops: Good. A couple of small UX asks: 1) please include expected failover behavior if peering drops (automatic routing fallback?), 2) we want a short rollback checklist (how we re-route traffic back to hosted endpoints).

Liam (Network): For peering outage there is no automatic fallback to hosted; we'd need to modify DNS and routes. We'll include a scripted rollback: update private-hosts record to point at hosted endpoint ENI and remove peer routes. We'll document step-by-step.

Maya (CS): I'll consolidate everything into a 1-pager runbook post-dry-run and tag legal for the KMS ownership clause. If no blockers after dry-run, react :thumbsup: and we'll lock the cutover date.

Isha (Security): Uploading final templates to ticket now.

Ruben (SRE): I'll be on-call during cutover window.

Strandline Ops: :thumbsup: thanks all, see you at the dry-run Friday.
